steps.title: Drawing with pyplot
steps.body:
**matplotlib.pyplot** draws charts. Call a plotting function, add a **title** and **labels**, then **plt.show()**.

In this app the finished picture appears as an **image** in the output panel under your text output.

steps.title: A line plot
steps.code:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

x = [1, 2, 3, 4]
y = [1, 4, 9, 16]
plt.plot(x, y, color="green", marker="o")
plt.title("Squares")
plt.show()
print("plot shown")

notes.text: plot draws a line; color and marker style it.
show renders the figure into the output panel.

steps.title: Bars and scatter in subplots
steps.code:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2)
axes[0].bar(["A", "B", "C"], [3, 5, 2])
axes[1].scatter([1, 2, 3], [3, 1, 2], color="purple")
fig.suptitle("Two plots")
plt.show()
print(len(axes))

notes.text: subplots makes one figure with a row of two axes.
Each axes object has its own plotting methods.

steps.title: Histogram, pie and counts
steps.code:
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

data = np.array([1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3, 4, 4, 5])
counts, edges = np.histogram(data, bins=4)
print(counts.tolist())
fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2)
ax1.hist(data, bins=4)
ax2.pie([30, 50, 20], labels=["x", "y", "z"])
plt.show()

notes.text: histogram counts values per bin without drawing.
hist draws the same bins as bars.

steps.title: Heatmaps and styling
steps.code:
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

grid = np.arange(12).reshape(3, 4)
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
im = ax.imshow(grid, cmap="viridis")
fig.colorbar(im)
ax.set_title("Heatmap")
ax.set_xlabel("column")
ax.set_ylabel("row")
plt.show()
print(grid.max())

notes.text: imshow draws a matrix as colored cells.

steps.question: Which call displays the figure in the output panel?
steps.explanation: plt.show() renders the current figures and the app displays them.

steps.question: How many axes does plt.subplots(2, 2) create?
steps.explanation: A 2 by 2 grid has four axes.

examples.title: Matplotlib: Line Plot
examples.description: Two styled lines with a legend.
examples.code:
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

x = np.linspace(0, 6.28, 100)
plt.plot(x, np.sin(x), label="sin", color="tab:blue")
plt.plot(x, np.cos(x), label="cos", color="tab:orange", linestyle="--")
plt.legend()
plt.title("Sine and cosine")
plt.show()
print("drawn")

examples.title: Matplotlib: Scatter
examples.code:
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
x = rng.random(40)
y = rng.random(40)
plt.scatter(x, y, c=x + y, cmap="plasma")
plt.colorbar()
plt.title("Scatter")
plt.show()
print(len(x), "points")

examples.title: Matplotlib: Bar Chart
examples.code:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

langs = ["Python", "Kotlin", "Rust"]
scores = [9, 8, 7]
plt.bar(langs, scores, color=["green", "purple", "orange"])
plt.ylabel("Score")
plt.title("Favorites")
plt.show()
print(max(scores))

examples.title: Matplotlib: Histogram
examples.code:
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
data = rng.normal(50, 10, 500)
plt.hist(data, bins=15, color="steelblue", edgecolor="white")
plt.title("Normal data")
plt.show()
print(round(data.mean()))

examples.title: Matplotlib: Box Plot
examples.code:
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

rng = np.random.default_rng(3)
groups = [rng.normal(m, 5, 60) for m in (10, 15, 20)]
plt.boxplot(groups)
plt.xticks([1, 2, 3], ["A", "B", "C"])
plt.title("Box plot")
plt.show()
print(len(groups))

examples.title: Matplotlib: Pie Chart
examples.code:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

labels = ["Rent", "Food", "Fun", "Savings"]
sizes = [40, 25, 15, 20]
plt.pie(sizes, labels=labels, autopct="%1.0f%%")
plt.title("Budget")
plt.show()
print(sum(sizes))

examples.title: Matplotlib: Heatmap
examples.code:
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

table = np.add.outer(np.arange(6), np.arange(6))
plt.imshow(table, cmap="magma")
plt.colorbar(label="row + column")
plt.title("Heatmap")
plt.show()
print(table.max())

examples.title: Matplotlib: Subplots
examples.code:
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

x = np.linspace(0, 5, 50)
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(7, 5))
axes[0, 0].plot(x, x)
axes[0, 1].plot(x, x ** 2, color="red")
axes[1, 0].bar([1, 2, 3], [3, 1, 2])
axes[1, 1].scatter(x, np.sin(x))
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
print(axes.shape)

examples.title: Matplotlib: Styling
examples.code:
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

x = np.linspace(0, 10, 200)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 4))
ax.plot(x, np.sin(x), color="crimson", linewidth=2.5)
ax.fill_between(x, np.sin(x), alpha=0.2, color="crimson")
ax.set_xlim(0, 10)
ax.set_ylim(-1.5, 1.5)
ax.grid(True, linestyle=":")
ax.annotate("peak", xy=(1.57, 1), xytext=(3, 1.25), arrowprops={"arrowstyle": "->"})
ax.set_title("Styled sine")
plt.show()
print("styled")
